title: The Messengership Of Prophet Muhammad 16th Degree 3rd Proof The Uniqueness Of Conveying The Message Summoning And Faith

questions.question: When many people fought against the Prophet’s message, how did he act?
questions.answer: He stayed brave and firm.

questions.question: Who are some groups that stood against him in this passage?
questions.answer: Big governments, other religions, and even his own people, tribe, and uncle.

questions.question: What does his success in spreading Islam show about him?
questions.answer: It shows he was very strong and special in giving the message.

questions.question: How strong was his faith?
questions.answer: His faith was amazingly strong and wide.

questions.question: What could not shake his faith?
questions.answer: The ideas, beliefs, and teachings around him could not make him doubt.

questions.question: Did fear or worry weaken his trust in Allah?
questions.answer: No. His trust stayed steady.

questions.question: Who learned from his faith after him?
questions.answer: The Companions and other holy believers in later times.

questions.question: What did those believers think about his level of faith?
questions.answer: They saw it as the highest level.

questions.question: What does the traveler decide about a person with such message, worship, prayer, calling, and faith?
questions.answer: Such a person would not lie or trick people.

questions.question: What is one main idea of this passage?
questions.answer: The Prophet was unmatched in courage and faith, so he was truthful.

questions.question: What job was the Prophet doing in this passage?
questions.answer: He was sharing Allah’s message and calling people to the truth.

questions.question: What good qualities did he show while doing that job?
questions.answer: He showed steadiness, strength, and courage.

questions.question: How do we know he did not back away?
questions.answer: He did not show fear, worry, or hesitation.

questions.question: Was opposition only from faraway people, or also from people close to him?
questions.answer: It was also from people close to him.

questions.question: What happened in the end when he called people to Islam?
questions.answer: Islam became powerful in the world.

questions.question: What word best tells about his faith: weak, unsure, or matchless?
questions.answer: Matchless.

questions.question: What kinds of things tried and failed to create doubt in him?
questions.answer: Popular beliefs, philosophers’ ideas, and religious teachings.

questions.question: Who are named as the first and strongest believers after him?
questions.answer: The Companions.

questions.question: From what picture does the passage say later believers took faith?
questions.answer: From his fountain of faith.

questions.question: Why does the traveler say lying does not fit him?
questions.answer: Because someone with such unique faith, worship, prayer, and truthfulness would not be false.

questions.question: In calling people to the truth, what three qualities are highlighted first?
questions.answer: Firmness, steadfastness, and courage.

questions.question: What makes his courage even more amazing?
questions.answer: So many enemies opposed him, even his own relatives and people.

questions.question: What did he not show, even a little?
questions.answer: He did not show doubt, fear, or nervousness.

questions.question: What result came from his struggle to spread the message?
questions.answer: He overcame the world’s challenge and Islam rose high.

questions.question: What does that result help prove?
questions.answer: It helps prove no one was like him in delivering the message.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the size and strength of his faith?
questions.answer: It says his faith was very strong, broad, and certain.

questions.question: What could the world’s strongest ideas not do to him?
questions.answer: They could not weaken his belief.

questions.question: Besides the Companions, who else drew from his belief?
questions.answer: The saintly people of all ages.

questions.question: What did those righteous people believe about his faith?
questions.answer: They believed his faith was the highest.

questions.question: What final judgment does the traveler make about him?
questions.answer: He is completely truthful, not deceitful.

questions.question: What was the Prophet inviting people to?
questions.answer: He was inviting them to the truth.

questions.question: How did he stay when others treated him with strong hate?
questions.answer: He stayed steady and courageous.

questions.question: Name one close person mentioned who opposed him.
questions.answer: His uncle.

questions.question: What does his victory over so much opposition show?
questions.answer: It shows great strength in his mission.

questions.question: What was special about his belief inside his heart?
questions.answer: It was full of certainty and trust.

questions.question: Could the teachings of others make him unsure?
questions.answer: No. They could not make him unsure.

questions.question: What feelings did not enter his faith?
questions.answer: Doubt, weakness, and anxiety.

questions.question: Which people are especially named as examples of strong believers who followed him?
questions.answer: His Companions.

questions.question: What big claim does the passage make about his faith compared to others?
questions.answer: It says no one’s faith was like his.

questions.question: After thinking about all this, what does the traveler believe about his honesty?
questions.answer: He believes falsehood and cheating do not belong to him.

questions.question: What hard situation did the Prophet face while sharing the message?
questions.answer: Many powerful groups and even his own people were against him.

questions.question: How did he respond to that hard situation?
questions.answer: He kept going without fear.

questions.question: What can we infer from his not wavering?
questions.answer: He truly believed in his message.

questions.question: What was unable to defeat his certainty?
questions.answer: The world’s ideas, beliefs, and teachings.

questions.question: What does this tell us about his trust in Allah?
questions.answer: His trust was very deep and strong.

questions.question: Who are said to have taken from his belief like people taking water from a spring?
questions.answer: The Companions and saintly people across time.

questions.question: The passage lists sacred law, Islam, worship, prayer, calling people, and faith. What do all these examples support?
questions.answer: They support that he was truthful.

questions.question: If someone is unique in all those good ways, what does the traveler say about lying?
questions.answer: Lying does not belong to such a person.

questions.question: What is the best short summary of the passage?
questions.answer: His courage and faith were unmatched, so his truthfulness is clear.

questions.question: What two big themes are taught in this passage?
questions.answer: His courage in sharing the message and his powerful faith.

questions.question: What kind of opposition did he face from his own side?
questions.answer: His own people, tribe, and uncle opposed him.

questions.question: Did this opposition make him stop or become shaky?
questions.answer: No. He remained firm.

questions.question: What happened to Islam through his work, according to the passage?
questions.answer: It became dominant in the world.

questions.question: How does the passage describe his certainty in belief?
questions.answer: It describes it as amazing and very high.

questions.question: What groups’ ideas could not plant doubt in him?
questions.answer: The ideas of common beliefs, wise thinkers, and religious leaders.

questions.question: Who are mentioned as reaching high levels of belief after him?
questions.answer: The Companions and saintly people of every age.

questions.question: What did those believers recognize in him?
questions.answer: They recognized the highest level of faith.

questions.question: What conclusion did the traveler reach with his mind?
questions.answer: He concluded that the Prophet could not be a liar or deceiver.

questions.question: Why is that conclusion made in this passage?
questions.answer: Because his law, religion, worship, prayer, call to truth, and faith were all unmatched.
